items.stem: Why is it misleading to describe 'AGI' as a single, precisely defined milestone that will clearly be reached on a known date?

options.text: AGI is a contested concept with no agreed definition or test, and expert timelines genuinely disagree
options.rationale: Correct: the term is used differently by different people and its arrival is deeply uncertain.

options.text: Because AGI has already been achieved and dated
options.rationale: Inaccurate: there is no agreed evidence of general intelligence today.

options.text: Because AGI is impossible and will never be discussed
options.rationale: Overstated: feasibility and timing are open, not closed, questions.

options.text: Because only one lab is allowed to define it
options.rationale: Inaccurate: no single body sets the definition.

items.explanation: Correct: the term is used differently by different people and its arrival is deeply uncertain.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about AI capability benchmarks are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A high benchmark score can overstate real-world ability if the test is narrow or leaked into training data
options.rationale: Correct: benchmarks measure specific tasks and can be gamed or contaminated.

options.text: Benchmarks measure narrow tasks and do not prove general understanding
options.rationale: Correct: performance on a test is not the same as general intelligence.

options.text: A benchmark score settles whether a system is generally intelligent
options.rationale: Incorrect: no single score demonstrates general intelligence.

options.text: Benchmarks are irrelevant and tell us nothing
options.rationale: Overstated: they are useful but limited and must be read carefully.

items.explanation: Correct: benchmarks measure specific tasks and can be gamed or contaminated.

items.stem: A commentator states a specific year by which AGI 'will definitely' arrive. How should this be treated?

options.text: As one uncertain opinion among many; timelines are contested and should carry explicit uncertainty
options.rationale: Correct: honest discussion of the future attaches confidence levels rather than certainty.

options.text: As established fact because an expert said it
options.rationale: Incorrect: expert disagreement is wide; authority is not certainty.

options.text: As impossible, since no change ever happens
options.rationale: Overstated: progress is real; its timing is what is uncertain.

options.text: As irrelevant because the future cannot be discussed at all
options.rationale: Incorrect: it can be discussed, carefully and with caveats.

items.explanation: Correct: honest discussion of the future attaches confidence levels rather than certainty.
